A hopeful fortnight guide for busy families
Readers usually want a clear answer
Aurelia Skyways Companion Animal Travel Desk

Traveling with a companion animal can feel stressful, but the process is usually smoother when you sort out the basics early. This guide gives you the main things to check before you arrive, so you can focus on the trip instead of last-minute surprises.

If your pet will fly in the cabin or in the hold, make sure the carrier fits the airline's rules and gives your animal enough space to stand, turn, and lie down. Keep the crate clean, secure, and well ventilated, and add familiar bedding only if it stays dry and does not block airflow. For cats, check the crate carefully and keep the largest side within the approved limit. <<FACT F067>> Bring any required travel papers, and keep them easy to show at check-in.

If you are traveling with a large dog, review the booking details early so you know what applies to that type of animal. <<FACT F057>> The Companion Animal Travel Desk can help you match the plan to the route, the aircraft, and the space available, which is especially useful when you are juggling children, bags, and a pet at the same time.

On the travel day, arrive a little early so you have room to settle your pet calmly. Offer water before leaving for the airport, but avoid a heavy meal right before departure unless your vet suggests otherwise. Keep a leash handy for any transfer points, and never open the carrier until a staff member says it is safe.

If your pet seems anxious, stay calm and speak softly. Supervisors listen carefully when a passenger is worried, and the team can help you understand the next step without making you feel rushed.

For more help with companion animal travel on Aurelia Skyways, contact the Companion Animal Travel Desk before you leave home.
